response:
Final-generation diagnosis. The archive now yields four robust conclusions. **(1) The champion mechanism is accrual-purged cash generation per dollar of capital formed** (`payback_on_gross_capital_formation`: fmb +4.12, alpha +0.050, talpha +5.58), and the gen-7 ablation proved the accrual purge — not earnings growth — supplies most of that power (removing it collapsed alpha to +0.023). **(2) The statistic matters as much as the ingredients:** replacing the endpoint-to-endpoint three-year difference with a deviation from the firm's own three-year norm (`cash_generation_above_own_norm_per_capital`) held fmb at +4.02 and alpha at +0.041 while lifting coverage from 0.085 to 0.111 — the single best coverage/strength trade in the archive. By contrast, the difference-in-differences numerator failed outright (fmb +0.80), so the *level* of cash improvement, not its excess over trend, is what is priced. **(3) Short-side asymmetry is now well documented:** inventory-based overhangs carry the spread (alpha −0.048 to −0.050, talpha ≈ −5) but flat slopes, while non-current soft-asset buckets show the mirror image (fmb −2.78, alpha −0.013) — the two are complementary in precisely the metric each lacks. **(4) Rank-blend composites add nothing** (gen 7 SUMRANK: Sharpe fell to 0.19), so any combination must be a single economic quantity on a common dollar scale. This final batch pairs the deviation statistic with the formation-based scale at high coverage, tests one ordinal robustness variant, and builds two dollar-scale fusions motivated by the complementarity in (3).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: deviation_payback_on_annual_formation
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), MA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), ADD(dp, ADD(ABS(DELTA(ppegt, 1)), ABS(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 1))))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual-adjusted cash generation above the firm's own recent norm, measured per dollar of capital the firm formed and consumed this year, is the cleanest available statement of productive versus accounting growth.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the one untested cell among the archive's three validated design choices: the deviation numerator (which raised coverage to 0.111 at fmb +4.02), the total-capital-formation deployment concept that charges acquired as well as built assets (which produced the best alpha, +0.050), and a strictly positive depreciation floor in the denominator that eliminates the ±1 pinning of asset-light firms. Matching an annual formation measure to an annual cash deviation also keeps the history requirement at three years, so it should deliver champion-level alpha at roughly 30% more observations than the 0.085-coverage payback family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: abnormal_self_financed_inventory_per_capacity
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(invt, SUB(lct, dlc)), ppegt), MA(RATIO(SUB(invt, SUB(lct, dlc)), ppegt), 3)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Goods held net of the supplier credit financing them, expressed per unit of installed productive capacity and compared to the firm's own norm, measures unsold output the firm's capacity cannot justify.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every short-side signal so far deviates a dollar amount and then scales it; this ratios first and deviates second, so the benchmark is the firm's own historical inventory-to-capacity relationship rather than its historical dollar level, which purges growth in firm size from the comparison entirely. That ordering is the untested structural choice in the strongest short-side family, and it directly targets the flat cross-sectional slopes (−0.95 to −1.58) that have accompanied its −0.05 alphas.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: own_history_rank_capital_productivity
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ADD(capx, dp)), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm currently at the top of its own five-year distribution of accrual-adjusted cash generation per dollar of capital deployed is running productive assets, while one near its own floor is carrying capital that is not producing cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The deviation-from-norm numerator worked because it uses all observations in the window rather than two endpoints; an ordinal own-history rank pushes that logic further by being completely insensitive to the magnitude of accounting outliers, which is the most likely residual source of noise in a ratio whose numerator contains an accrual difference. It is a genuinely different statistic — a within-firm quantile rather than a scaled dollar deviation — and it needs no winsorization, so it also serves as a robustness check on whether the payback result survives when only the ordering of a firm's own history is used.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: cash_deviation_net_of_inventory_build
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), MA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), ADD(capx, dp)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The best firms generate cash above their own norm without accumulating self-financed inventory; the worst do the reverse, and both conditions belong in one dollar-denominated measure rather than in two separately ranked signals.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's strongest long-side channel (cash deviation per capital deployed, fmb +4.02) and strongest short-side channel (self-financed inventory build per capital deployed, alpha −0.050 at talpha −5.41) share an identical scale, so they can be netted as dollars in a single numerator — which is exactly what the failed SUMRANK composite could not do without the size and distribution distortions the critic identified. If the two channels are complementary rather than overlapping, this should exceed both parents on alpha and talpha at 0.111 coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: total_soft_asset_overhang
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(invt, MA(invt, 3)), SUB(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 3))), ADD(capx, dp)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Unreversed soft-asset accumulation is one economic phenomenon spanning the balance sheet — unsold goods in current assets and capitalized costs in non-current assets — and summing both overhangs on a common capital scale should predict returns more reliably than either alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two buckets have exactly complementary weaknesses in the archive: abnormal inventory delivers alpha −0.048 with talpha −5.02 but a slope of only −1.58, while abnormal capitalized costs deliver a slope of −2.78 with an alpha of just −0.013. Because both are measured with the same own-norm deviation device and the same capx-plus-depreciation scale, adding them is a single overhang quantity rather than a blend of differently distributed signals, and the pooled measure should inherit the slope from one leg and the spread from the other.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: full_purge_deviation_payback
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), MA(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, act), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1)), 3)), ADD(dp, ADD(ABS(DELTA(ppegt, 1)), ABS(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 1))))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: If purge completeness is what drives the payback family, then removing non-current operating accruals as well as working-capital accruals from the cash measure should improve the deviation-based, formation-scaled specification just as it improved the endpoint-based, capex-scaled one.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Paired with Signal 1, this isolates a single design choice — purge depth — while holding the statistic and the scale fixed, which is the cleanest remaining test of the mechanism the gen-7 ablation identified as the family's engine. The comparison matters for interpretation rather than merely for score: if the deeper purge helps here as it did with the capex denominator (fmb +4.32 versus +3.60), the theme interaction is confirmed as operating through total accrual content, and if it does not, the effect is specifically a working-capital phenomenon.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE deviation_payback_on_annual_formation---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a denominator relabeling of the existing archive champion `cash_generation_above_own_norm_per_capital` — ABS(Δppegt)+dp is a near-substitute for capx+dp for most firms — so the only genuine increment is charging intangible formation, which is too thin a change to count as a substantively different specification rather than a cosmetic variant.

---CRITIQUE abnormal_self_financed_inventory_per_capacity---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Ratio-first-then-deviate is a genuinely different statistic from the archive's deviate-then-scale short-side family and the sign is coherent, but the label "supplier credit" is wrong (lct−dlc sweeps in accrued expenses and taxes payable, not just payables) and the raw ppegt denominator will pin asset-light firms in the tails despite winsorization.

---CRITIQUE own_history_rank_capital_productivity---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: An ordinal within-firm rank of the same underlying quantity is close to a transform of an already-tested signal, but it discards level information entirely and is outlier-immune, so it is a legitimate — if low-upside — robustness test rather than a mere restatement.

---CRITIQUE cash_deviation_net_of_inventory_build---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Internally inconsistent: the accrual-adjusted cash numerator already subtracts Δ(act−che) and adds Δ(lct−dlc), so netting (Δinvt − Δ(lct−dlc)) again double-weights inventory build and puts a 2× coefficient on current liabilities, and it mixes a deviation-from-norm term with a raw one-year change on unequal footing.

---CRITIQUE total_soft_asset_overhang---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Pooling two own-norm overhangs measured in the same units on the same capital scale is a coherent composite rather than a rank blend, though the claim that it will inherit the slope of one leg and the alpha of the other is wishful — an unweighted dollar sum will simply be dominated by whichever bucket is larger in each firm.

---CRITIQUE full_purge_deviation_payback---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The purge-depth comparison was already run in the archive (`synthetic_cashflow_payback` +3.60 vs `full_accrual_adjusted_payback` +4.32), so re-running it on a denominator that is itself a cosmetic variant yields a diagnostic that largely restates a known result rather than testing a new mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: cash_gain_per_soft_asset_base
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), MA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), ADD(dp, SUB(SUB(SUB(at, che), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The right thing to divide a cash improvement by is not the capital the firm deployed but the stock of accounting assets that improvement has to justify — receivables, inventory and capitalized costs — because those are the claims most at risk of reversal.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This is a change of economic concept rather than a relabeling: capx+dp and ABS(Δppegt)+dp both measure capital *deployed*, whereas the denominator here is the soft-asset *stock carried*, formed as total assets less cash, plant and purchased intangibles, which is a different quantity that is large exactly for the accounting-growth firms the theme targets and small for capital-intensive real investors. The result therefore answers a question no archive entry addresses — whether cash generation should be benchmarked against real deployment or against the accounting balances that must be worked off — while keeping the validated deviation numerator and its 0.111 coverage.
REASONING: Adding depreciation gives the denominator a strictly positive floor so asset-light firms with negligible soft assets are not pinned at extreme values.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: cash_gain_net_of_inventory_overhang
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), MA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), SUB(SUB(invt, MA(invt, 3)), SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), MA(SUB(lct, dlc), 3)))), ADD(capx, dp)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm deserves credit only for cash generated above its own norm that is not accompanied by a standing, self-financed inventory overhang; the two conditions are one economic test and belong in a single dollar-denominated measure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The double-counting is eliminated by replacing the one-year inventory build — which the accrual-adjusted cash numerator already contains — with the *level* overhang relative to the firm's own three-year norm, a stock statistic that no cash-flow term includes, so inventory now enters once as a flow inside the cash measure and once as an accumulated position outside it. Both terms are now deviations from own norms on the same dollar scale, which fixes the unequal-footing objection, and the construction unites the archive's strongest long-side statistic (fmb +4.02) with its strongest short-side statistic (alpha −0.048, talpha −5.02) as one quantity rather than a rank blend that gen 7 showed adds nothing.
REASONING: Netting the payables overhang preserves the self-financing distinction that made the inventory channel work.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: soft_asset_burden_per_cash_generated
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(at, che), ppent), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(dp, ABS(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Firms carrying a large stock of accounting assets per dollar of accrual-adjusted cash they generate are running businesses whose balance sheets have outgrown their cash-generating capability, and they subsequently underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The purge-depth question was indeed already settled, so this slot instead inverts the family's entire orientation: every archive signal is a flow-over-deployment payback, whereas this is a stock-over-cash burden — how many years of cash generation the soft asset base represents — which is a level characteristic rather than an improvement measure and is therefore the natural short-side complement to the payback family. Using accrual-adjusted cash flow rather than earnings in the denominator keeps the measure cross-theme, and the depreciation floor plus absolute value keeps it defined and monotone for firms with weak or negative cash generation.
REASONING: All inputs are one-year balance-sheet and income items, so coverage should be at the high end of the archive rather than the 0.085 of the three-year payback signals.
